title: feat: terminal-style auth status (login not available yet)
body:
## Summary

Visitors previously hit a provider picker (or a plain GitHub button) when trying to sign in, with no clear signal that public login is closed. This adds a **terminal-style auth status** that communicates login isn't live yet, in a way that matches cribble's CRT/hacker aesthetic without looking generic.

New `AuthStatus` component (`src/components/AuthStatus.tsx`), rendered in an **amber "standby" CRT tone** that's deliberately distinct from the site's green "live" signal:

- **`AuthStatusBoard`** — a fake `cribble@auth-gateway` terminal that "runs" `cribble auth --status`, printing staggered health-check lines (`resolving identity service … ok`, `requesting public handshake … refused`, provider `STANDBY`/`OFFLINE` tags) ending in a blinking `LOGIN IS NOT LIVE YET`.
- **`AuthStatusPill`** — a small clickable `AUTH · OFFLINE` pill with a pulsing diode.
- **`AuthStatusModal`** — a popup with the board + a "get notified when it opens" CTA that jumps to the waitlist.

### Where it shows
- **Landing page** — `Register` / `Sign In` now open the status popup (instead of the old register modal), and a status pill sits under the CTAs.
- **`/login`** — the board explains public sign-in isn't open yet; the GitHub button is kept behind a `HAVE A BETA INVITE?` divider so the beta path still works, plus a waitlist link.

All animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Removed the now-unused register modal + provider marks from the landing page.

## Test plan

- [ ] Landing: the `AUTH · OFFLINE` pill opens the same popup.

title: fix: loading screen animation stuck on reload

## Summary

Inline styles referenced a scoped/hashed keyframe name that never matched, so nothing animated. The dot also referenced a `pulse` keyframe that doesn't exist in this scope.
- Moved the animations into styled-jsx classes (`loading-dot`, `loading-dash`) so the keyframes resolve correctly, and added a proper `dot-pulse` keyframe for the status dot.

title: Add "better on a laptop" notice for mobile visitors on /login
body: ## What Mobile visitors on `/login` now see a dismissible notice explaining that the cribble browser extension isn't available on mobile, and that they should switch to a PC or laptop for the full experience. [Mobile login with notice](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-019f74e8-71fb-76ce-a7e5-56ef4d704b5e/artifacts?path=%2Ftmp%2Flogin-mobile.png) ## How - New `MobileDeviceNotice` component (`src/components/login/MobileDeviceNotice.tsx`), rendered just above the auth panel on the login page. - Device detection uses the `(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)` media query rather than viewport width, so a narrow desktop window is never flagged and touchscreen laptops (which expose a fine pointer) stay exempt. Detection runs in an effect, so SSR and the first client render agree and there is no hydration mismatch. - The notice is informational, not a blocker — sign-in still works on mobile. Dismissing it (X button) hides it for the rest of the browser session via `sessionStorage`. - Styling reuses the page's existing motifs (`glass-pop` panel, `lg-rise` entrance, mono eyebrow, accent icon) so it blends into the login aesthetic. ## Verification - `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run build` all pass. - Verified in headless Chrome against a production build: - iPhone emulation (touch + mobile): notice renders with the expected copy; dismissing removes it and it stays hidden after reload. - Desktop at 1280px and at a narrow 420px window (mouse pointer): notice does not render. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

title: Default desktop navigation to the left command rail
body: New and unset devices now open the app with the left command rail on desktop. The top bar remains available in Appearance, and an explicit Top bar choice is still persisted. ## Why The product default was the sticky top bar. The left rail is the intended desktop chrome; this flips the fallback so users who have not picked a position get the rail. ## What changed - `resolveNavPosition` treats missing or invalid `cribble.nav.pos` as `left` - The pre-paint boot script uses the same fallback, so the content inset matches on first load - Appearance copy notes that the left rail is the default - Devices that already stored `top` keep the top bar ## How to verify 1. Clear `localStorage` (or use a fresh profile) and open any authenticated page at ≥768px — the left rail should be the chrome 2. Settings → Appearance → Top bar, reload — top bar should stick 3. Switch back to Left rail, reload — rail should stick 4. Below 768px the top bar / drawer fallback should still appear in rail mode

title: fix: resolve /favicon.ico public-vs-page conflict
body: GET `/favicon.ico` 500'd on localhost because Next.js found both: - `src/app/favicon.ico` (App Router metadata file → `/favicon.ico`) - `public/favicon.ico` (static file → the same path) That is the [conflicting-public-file-page](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/conflicting-public-file-page) error. The brand pipeline already treats `src/app/favicon.ico` as the ICO source of truth (`public/favicon.png` and `public/apple-icon.png` stay for the extra sizes in root metadata). This removes the extra public ICO, documents the constraint in `scripts/make-brand-assets.mjs`, and adds a regression test so both files cannot land together again. title: Quiet the shop: product-first plates, less costume
body: The shop was over-costumed. The first pass fixed the noise but sanded off the character. This is where it lands: quiet chrome, loud moments. ## What changed - **Header** is ANSI Shadow `SHOP`, same family as Bag and Dashboard, with `// PLATES FOR THE BOARD · RANK STAYS EARNED`. - **Team / Billboard / Manage** are a small right-aligned utility rail — three chips, gold dot on Team. They read as doors out of the store, not products. - **Fan** still deals from a stacked deck. Art, name, rarity. - **Pro** gets its arcade back: gold keyline with a slow idle sheen, hatched panel surface, `CRIBBLE PRO` pixel wordmark, gold `+` perks, LED price digits that roll in per glyph, `BEST VALUE` tag, and the `GO PRO` button with its sheen sweep and nudging arrow. The digits are true gold now, not the old acid `#fcff00`. The plate-art backdrop stays gone — that was the readability problem. - **Mythic** flagship fills its tall cell with the scene notes that were cut ("Every 45 seconds the crack gives and blinding light floods through the sky"), a framed art stage, and a spec row. Koi and Horizon stay compact. - **Founder / Champion** take gold ink again. - **Section heads** carry the `//` mono marker in accent. **Personality budget:** accent green is system chrome (ASCII, `//`), gold is premium only (Pro, Team, Founder, Champion), plate accent belongs to plate cards, and pixel font is numerals and tags only — never body copy. ## What did not change - Polar checkout / portal / cosmetics APIs - PlateLayer scenes, prices, plate IDs, Pro discount math - Premium welcome modal behavior ## Performance and a11y Every new animation is transform or opacity only and gates off under `data-perf="low"`, `prefers-reduced-motion`, and `html[data-motion="reduced"]`. The stage observer still pauses off-screen plate scenes. Prices stay `aria-hidden`; the accessible amount rides the CTA's `aria-label`. ## Review Start at `/shop` in dark, then light, then narrow (rail wraps, mythics stack in catalog order). title: Model provider attribution separately from agent harness usage
body:
## Problem

Cribble's current Agent payload distinguishes local harnesses (`agents[]`) and model names (`models[]`), but it has no explicit model-provider dimension and does not transmit per-model token counts.

That makes several different requests easy to conflate:

1. local harness support, such as Hermes Agent, Codex, OpenCode, or Gemini CLI;
2. inference-provider attribution, such as OpenRouter or Nous Portal;
3. importing a provider's authoritative billing/usage ledger.

The bundled ccusage release already supports many local harnesses, including Hermes, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Grok, and others. OpenRouter and Nous Portal are providers, not harnesses. Their usage may be visible only as model names in local logs, or through separate provider APIs.

A second aggregator such as tokenmaxxing is also not a source of inference. Importing its totals without lineage could double-count the same ccusage sessions.

## Proposed design

Define provider attribution separately from harness identity:

```text
source/harness: hermes | codex | opencode | ...
provider: anthropic | openai | openrouter | nous | ... | unknown
model: provider-native model identifier
provenance: local_session | provider_ledger
```

Before adding direct portal imports, define a deduplication identity so a local Hermes session routed through OpenRouter is not counted again when an OpenRouter billing record is imported.

## Suggested phases

1. Preserve provider metadata when the local harness log exposes it.
2. Extend the wire/storage/read schemas with provider and per-model/provider totals while remaining backward compatible with schema v1.
3. Add an explicit source registry and capability matrix to `cribble-agent`.
4. Evaluate opt-in direct imports for OpenRouter and Nous Portal using scoped read-only credentials, separate from the Cribble Agent key.
5. Publish reconciliation diagnostics for unknown provider and potential duplicates.

## Acceptance questions

- Is provider attribution intended for the private dashboard, public Burn Board, or both?
- What is the canonical identity for deduplicating local session usage against provider-ledger usage?
- Should provider cost use authoritative billed cost when available and ccusage estimates otherwise?
- How should subscription-included usage be distinguished from API-equivalent estimates?

This issue was prepared with AI assistance after reviewing the current ccusage-based collector and schema-v1 Agent payload. No provider credentials or private usage data were used.

title: Add gamified Playstyles for burn, budget, and adaptive model routing
body:
## Problem

Cribble makes token usage playful and competitive, but users currently have to choose model strategy outside the product. I want to switch intentionally between multiple accounts and agents depending on the goal:

- spend aggressively when chasing the Burn Board or frontier quality;
- stay inside a hard budget when money or subscription allowance is tight; or
- reserve smarter models for planning and review while routing implementation, tests, commands, docs, and commits to efficient models.

That pattern applies across Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents, but each exposes different configuration and orchestration controls. Cribble should not claim it applied a strategy unless the corresponding harness adapter can prove it.

## Product concept: Playstyles

Add a private Playstyle surface to the token dashboard with three presets:

### Max Burn

Use high-capability models broadly. Optimize for leaderboard placement and maximum quality rather than token efficiency.

### Broke Mode

Use strong models for strategy and review, efficient or local models for implementation and testing, and low-cost models for mechanical work such as docs and commits. Track a user-selected budget target.

### Tactician

Escalate to premium models only when ambiguity, risk, or failed evidence justifies it. This is the balanced default.

Users should eventually be able to clone a preset into a custom Playstyle.

## Product placement

Playstyle selection belongs in the private token-usage dashboard because it is a personal strategy, budget, and configuration decision. The public Burn Board should continue ranking actual usage. A user may optionally display a Playstyle badge later, but self-selected modes must not change token totals or ranking math.

The private dashboard can gamify both strategies without inventing a productivity score:

- Max Burn streaks and burn milestones;
- under-budget streaks;
- premium-model concentration in strategy/review;
- efficient-model concentration in mechanical work;
- reconciliation and duplicate-source warnings.

Budget achievements should measure adherence and routing composition, not claim task quality or productivity per token.

## Delivery phases

This issue describes the complete product direction, but implementation should land through small, independently reviewable pull requests.

### Phase 1: recommendation-only dashboard

- show the active or selected Playstyle;
- explain role-based routing recommendations;
- preview expected model roles and budget behavior;
- track private budget targets and usage composition;
- do not edit agent configuration or claim enforcement.

### Phase 2: portable Playstyle policy

Define a small versioned policy around four public roles:

```text
Strategist: architecture, planning, ambiguous debugging
Builder: implementation
Utility: tests, commands, docs, commits, mechanical work
Reviewer: independent verification and escalation
```

A policy maps task class, risk, and remaining budget to one of those roles and a model tier. It should not encode one user's private skills, model names, paths, or accounts.

### Phase 3: Cribble Agent preview and status

Add a safe interface such as:

```text
cribble playstyle list
cribble playstyle use broke --preview
cribble playstyle status
cribble playstyle rollback
```

Preview must show exact proposed changes. Unsupported harnesses remain recommendation-only.

### Phase 4: Hermes adapter

Hermes is the first active adapter because profiles, delegation, and role-specific model routing already provide a natural application surface. Applying a Playstyle must be explicit, reversible, and verifiable.

### Phase 5: Claude Code and Codex

Start with validated configuration exports. Add active adapters only where each harness exposes a stable, safe, reversible configuration surface.

### Phase 6: intelligent routing

Use task class, risk, ambiguity, failed verification, context size, and remaining budget to recommend or apply escalation. The policy should route docs and commits differently from architecture or security review without pretending a cheap model preserved quality when no outcome evidence exists.

## Safety and truthfulness

- Never edit arbitrary dotfolders without a preview, backup, and rollback path.
- Never claim a Playstyle is active unless the adapter verifies the effective state.
- Keep credentials and account identifiers out of policies and public views.
- Keep detailed model/account usage private by default.
- Do not create a public efficiency leaderboard until Cribble has reliable, non-gameable outcome-quality evidence.
- Preserve actual Burn Board accounting regardless of selected Playstyle.

## Initial acceptance criteria

- The private dashboard can represent Max Burn, Broke Mode, and Tactician without changing public ranking math.
- Phase 1 clearly labels recommendations as recommendations rather than applied configuration.
- A Playstyle policy separates Strategist, Builder, Utility, and Reviewer roles.
- Budget targets and streaks use private, factual usage data.
- Later active adapters must support preview, explicit apply, status verification, and rollback.
- Implementation is split into narrow PRs by phase and harness.

Prepared with AI assistance after reviewing Cribble's current private token dashboard, Burn Board, Cribble Agent configuration model, and existing provider-attribution issue #46.

title: Track token usage from local LLM runtimes such as Ollama and llama.cpp
body:
## Problem

Cribble tracks coding-agent token usage through `cribble-agent`, primarily via ccusage plus a supplemental Prime Agent reader. That covers many hosted-model harnesses, but it does not account for inference performed directly by local runtimes such as Ollama or llama.cpp.

This makes local Qwen, Llama, Gemma, DeepSeek, and similar workloads effectively invisible even when they perform substantial coding-agent work. It also biases the Burn Board and private usage dashboard toward metered providers.

Current constraints observed on main:

- the server accepts only `source: "ccusage"`;
- `cribble-agent` has an additive-reader pattern for sources ccusage does not cover;
- the existing provider-attribution proposal in #46 separates harness, provider, model, and provenance, which this should build on rather than duplicate;
- local inference has real token usage but usually zero provider-billed cost, so tokens and cost must remain separate facts.

## Proposed direction

Add an opt-in local-inference collector to `cribble-agent`, starting with Ollama's local API and designed around a provider-neutral event contract that can later support llama.cpp or other OpenAI-compatible local servers.

Example normalized event:

```text
source/harness: hermes | opencode | custom | unknown
provider/runtime: ollama | llama.cpp | local-openai-compatible
model: qwen3:32b | llama3.3:70b | ...
provenance: local_runtime_ledger
tokens:
  input
  output
  cache_read/cache_write/reasoning when explicitly reported
cost:
  billed_usd: 0
  estimate_kind: local_unmetered
occurred_at / request_id / runtime_instance_id
```

The initial implementation should consume authoritative runtime counters where available, not tokenize prompts heuristically. For Ollama, request/stream completion metadata exposes prompt and generation evaluation counts; the collector needs a durable local ledger or proxy hook because polling the model list alone cannot reconstruct historical usage.

## Accounting and privacy requirements

- Keep token totals independent from monetary cost. `0 billed cost` must not mean `0 usage`.
- Do not upload prompts, responses, file paths, hostnames, IP addresses, or model weights.
- Keep collection opt-in and read-only from Cribble's perspective.
- Define deduplication before combining runtime events with Hermes/OpenCode/other session logs that may describe the same request.
- Preserve timestamped per-event facts so timezone buckets and model shares remain exact.
- Distinguish unknown token classes rather than manufacturing cache or reasoning counts.
- Bound local reads, validate integer ranges, reject malformed/partial ledgers, and make foreground/background collection consistent.

## Suggested phases

1. Extend schema/source capability handling beyond the current `ccusage` literal while remaining backward compatible.
2. Define a local-runtime event and deduplication identity compatible with #46.
3. Add an opt-in Ollama adapter with synthetic fixtures and a real local smoke test.
4. Surface local models in private token usage and public Burn Board totals with `billed cost = 0` clearly represented.
5. Add llama.cpp/OpenAI-compatible local runtimes after the Ollama contract is proven.

## Acceptance criteria

- A local Qwen request through Ollama contributes exact prompt/output tokens to Cribble.
- The same request is not double-counted when a coding harness also records it.
- Hosted and local token totals use the same token-class semantics where available.
- Local usage appears in agent/model breakdowns without inventing provider spend.
- No prompt, completion, machine identity, or local network details leave the machine.
- Foreground sync and scheduled background sync produce the same result.
- Malformed, duplicated, or partially written local events fail closed rather than silently changing totals.

Related: #46 provider attribution and provider-ledger reconciliation.

Prepared with AI assistance after reviewing current Cribble and `cribble-agent` main. No private usage data or credentials were used.

title: Roadmap: layered agentic quality and CI hardening
body:
## Why

Issue #3 established the quality/security goal and the existing CI now covers install, production dependency audit, lint, typecheck, 944 tests, build, selected pages, response headers, and two API contracts. A read-only execution audit at `d0b91c82d54a19e1da2d361d19016e7d7c39bd17` found several independent failure classes that those gates do not cover. This issue proposes small, separately reviewable additions rather than one kitchen-sink workflow.

## Measured baseline

Local serial baseline (Node 20.19.5/npm 10.8.2): `npm ci` 45.9s; production audit 1.9s; lint 31.8s; typecheck 92.8s; tests 26.9s; placeholder-env build 173.8s. All passed. Recent GitHub CI was materially faster, so each PR below should publish its own runner delta instead of relying on these local timings.

Tool trials were exact-version, local/no-account runs. No source, credentials, or unredacted findings were uploaded.

## Roadmap by enforcement lane

### Fast required PR checks

- [x] **Workflow integrity** — actionlint 1.7.12 plus zizmor 1.29.0, offline, with every action/executable pinned. Measured cold local runtime: 2.05s. Sabotage proves malformed expressions and unpinned actions fail. Set `persist-credentials: false` for checkout steps that do not push. Implemented in #64.
- [ ] **Secret diff** — Gitleaks 8.30.1 against merge-base..head with redaction. The audit found two placeholder false positives (`.env.example` and CI placeholder), so add only narrow path/rule allowlists; do not blanket-ignore generic keys. Synthetic service-role-token sabotage must fail without printing the token. Follow with a scheduled redacted history scan.

### Advisory/baselined PR checks

- [ ] **Unused wiring** — Knip 6.32.3 found 38 files, 75 exports, 3 dependencies and 1 unlisted dependency in 7.18s. Configure script/Next entrypoints, commit reviewed fingerprints, keep legacy findings visible, and fail only new findings after review.
- [ ] **Public browser contract** — Playwright 1.62.1 + axe-core 4.13.0 at 360x800 and 1440x900. The 18.7s audit found Vercel analytics console/network failures plus serious `aria-prohibited-attr` findings that status-only smoke missed. Establish an explicit expiring baseline, then fail new serious/critical axe, unexpected console/network, status, and overflow regressions.
- [ ] **Changed critical-module coverage** — publish coverage JSON and ratchet reviewed critical modules; do not impose a gameable global percentage on the current 16.04% line coverage.

### Scheduled deep checks

- [ ] **Developer/build-chain vulnerabilities** — OSV-Scanner 2.5.1 found 35 vulnerability groups across 12 packages while `npm audit --omit=dev` passed. Run on lockfile changes and nightly; record explicit owner/expiry for reviewed exceptions.
- [ ] **Architecture** — dependency-cruiser 18.2.0 only after committed cycle/boundary rules, Node 22 isolation, a `totalCruised > 0` assertion, and a cycle sabotage. The bare `src` invocation silently scanned zero modules, so never treat an empty graph as green.
- [ ] **SAST** — GitHub CodeQL JavaScript/TypeScript *or* a tiny vendored Semgrep ruleset, not both. The Semgrep trial returned exit 0 despite malformed-rule/parser errors; any wrapper must fail when its errors array is non-empty.
- [ ] **Database and route contracts** — disposable migration replay/bootstrap diff/RLS/grant assertions; generated schema/type drift; a route manifest covering method/auth/status/content-type/body semantics. Current CI samples 2 of 97 API route files.
- [ ] **Mutation/performance hotspots** — bounded Node-22 Stryker target for score/auth boundaries; three-run filesystem-only LHCI medians; jscpd/selected aislop findings as human hotspot reports, not aggregate gates.

### Release-only gates

- [ ] Promote an already-tested artifact; production-like short-lived credentials; migration preflight; authenticated critical flows; webhook/cron auth; desktop/mobile/keyboard browser contracts; route bundle budgets. Keep Lighthouse advisory until variance is characterized.

## Baseline and safety contract

- Fingerprint exact commit, tool version, rule, normalized path/location; unchanged legacy debt remains visible with owner and expiry.
- Rebaseline only in a dedicated reviewed diff. Never baseline exposed secrets, critical security, unresolved imports/build/type/test, migration replay, auth/RLS, or route-contract failures.
- Basic fork-PR checks get `contents: read`, no repository credentials after checkout, no secrets, no comment bot, no SARIF/source upload, no telemetry, and offline modes where supported.
- Pin actions by full commit SHA and downloaded executables by version plus SHA-256. No floating `npx`, tags, or curl-pipe installers.
- Every gate lands with deterministic sabotage, measured cold runtime, and an explicit failure policy.

## Explicit non-goals

Do not add overlapping required linters for fashion. React Doctor 0.9.12 (390 findings, 200.6s, ambiguous license metadata), aggregate aislop (652 overlapping/noisy diagnostics), broad jscpd, broad Semgrep, size-limit without a real artifact budget, global coverage, full-repository mutation, Biome/Oxlint/Madge/TruffleHog are not proposed as required PR gates.

This roadmap refines and extends #3; it does not claim authenticated flows, hosted CodeQL, Vercel deployment, or database replay currently pass.

title: Add contextual sharing for personalized leaderboard results
body:
## User story

As a Burn Board participant, I want to share the exact leaderboard result I am looking at, not a generic leaderboard homepage.

For example, I am currently first place for weekly AI-token usage. I want a Share action beside my result that creates a useful link preview showing that result. When someone opens the link, Cribble should restore the Token tab and weekly window, locate my public row, scroll it into view, and visibly focus it. The same contract should work if I am fifteenth rather than first.

This should eventually become the shared behavior for contextual links across Cribble: preserve the useful page state and the specific public object or result being shared.

## Product contract

A shared leaderboard result needs three separate pieces:

1. **Stable target identity**
   - Deep-link to a public username/user slug, not rank alone, because ranks move.
   - Include the selected board and time window, for example Token Board + week.
   - Resolve the person's current rank when the link is opened.

2. **Context restoration**
   - Open `/leaderboard` on the correct tab and time window.
   - After data loads, scroll the targeted row into view.
   - Apply a bounded focus/highlight treatment so the recipient can tell what was shared.
   - If the user is no longer present on that public board, keep the board usable and show a neutral unavailable-result state rather than focusing the wrong row.

3. **Personalized link preview**
   - The Open Graph/social image should represent the shared public result, not a generic Cribble image.
   - Include the public display name, board name, current rank, selected time window, token total, and a clear capture timestamp or “as of” label.
   - Never include private usage events, machine/account identifiers, API keys, or data beyond the existing opt-in public Burn Board aggregate.
   - The preview must not imply that a rank is permanent.

## Easiest vertical slice

Start with the Token tab of `/leaderboard`:

- Add a Share button beside the authenticated user's public result.
- Generate a deterministic contextual URL carrying:
  - `view=tokens`
  - the active time window
  - a stable public user target
- Use `navigator.share()` when available and copy-to-clipboard as the fallback.
- On open, restore the Token tab/window, wait for the matching row, call `scrollIntoView`, and apply the existing bounded row-highlight/ignition language.
- Preserve normal back/forward behavior and do not select a stale row when filters or data change.

A concrete URL shape can be selected during implementation. The contract matters more than whether it uses query parameters, a hash, or a dedicated share route.

## Follow-up slices

### Personalized Open Graph image

Add a server-resolved share route or metadata/image endpoint that can render the public result at request time and then land the recipient on the contextual leaderboard target.

### Additional result targets

Extend the same contract to:

- another public player's row;
- AI-tool and team boards;
- podium cards or other public result objects;
- other Cribble pages where a generic URL loses the context the user intended to share.

### Native browser sharing

Browser chrome shares the current URL and cannot be intercepted reliably by page code. If Cribble should support that path, keep the URL synchronized only with an explicitly selected/focused share target. Avoid rewriting history continuously during ordinary scrolling.

## Initial acceptance criteria

- [ ] A signed-in, opted-in Burn Board participant sees Share beside their public Token Board result.
- [ ] Sharing uses the active board and time window plus a stable public user identity.
- [ ] Opening the URL restores the Token tab and window, scrolls the matching row into view, and highlights it.
- [ ] Rank changes do not break the link or focus a different person.
- [ ] Missing/non-public targets fail neutrally without exposing private state.
- [ ] Web Share API and clipboard fallback both preserve the same URL.
- [ ] Back/forward navigation and existing leaderboard loading/error behavior remain intact.
- [ ] Tests cover first place, a below-the-fold rank such as fifteenth, rank movement, missing target, and clipboard fallback.
- [ ] A later OG-image slice uses public aggregate data only and labels the result with a capture time.

## Relevant current surfaces

- `src/app/(app)/leaderboard/page.tsx` owns board-tab selection.
- `src/components/leaderboard/TokenBoard.tsx` owns the Burn Board, current-user row, and existing row highlight behavior.
- `src/components/leaderboard/TokenPlayerCard.tsx` owns token-result presentation.
- `src/app/api/leaderboard/tokens/route.ts` provides the public aggregate.

Prepared with AI assistance after inspecting the current leaderboard route, Token Board components, public-token API, repository issue/PR inventory, and existing Burn Board privacy contract. Product direction and user story are Kevin's.

title: Show project icons for Pi, OpenCode, and other recognized harnesses
body:
## Problem

The Burn Board and profile agent surfaces render a branded icon for a small fixed set of harnesses, but recognized harnesses such as **Pi** and **OpenCode** fall back to a generic letter tile instead of their project icon.

OpenCode is already normalized by `tokenAgentLabel` (`opencode` / `open-code` → `OpenCode`), but `TokenAgentIcon` has no corresponding branded visual. Pi is not yet represented consistently in the collector-label/icon mapping. This makes valid agent attribution look incomplete even when Cribble has the harness name.

## User story

As a Burn Board participant, I want every recognized coding harness in my token breakdown to show its correct project icon so I can distinguish Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, Claude Code, and other harnesses at a glance.

## Proposed contract

- Add a centralized, tested harness-brand registry shared by all `TokenAgentIcon` consumers.
- Support at least these collector aliases:
  - `pi`, `pi-agent`, `pi-coding-agent` → **Pi**
  - `opencode`, `open-code` → **OpenCode**
- Render project-supplied assets sourced from authoritative brand/project repositories, with provenance and licensing recorded in the repository.
- Preserve the current generic, deterministic fallback for unknown harnesses.
- A missing or failed image must fall back without layout shift, broken-image chrome, or an empty icon.
- Keep labels and visuals consistent across the Burn Board, token player card, profile agent breakdown, and player modal.
- Do not conflate harness identity with model/provider identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pi aliases normalize to `Pi` and render the Pi icon.
- [ ] OpenCode aliases continue to normalize to `OpenCode` and render the OpenCode icon.
- [ ] Existing Hermes and other branded harness icons remain unchanged.
- [ ] Unknown harnesses retain the current generic initial fallback.
- [ ] Image-load failure has a tested visual fallback.
- [ ] All `TokenAgentIcon` call sites use the same registry.
- [ ] Asset source, revision/URL, and license or permitted brand-use basis are documented.
- [ ] Tests cover aliases, known-brand asset selection, unknown fallback, and failed-image fallback.

## Relevant current surfaces

- `src/components/leaderboard/TokenAgentIcon.tsx`
- `src/lib/tokenLeaderboard.ts`
- `src/lib/tokenLeaderboard.test.ts`
- `src/components/leaderboard/TokenBoard.tsx`
- `src/components/leaderboard/TokenPlayerCard.tsx`
- `src/components/leaderboard/PlayerCard.tsx`
- `src/app/(app)/u/[username]/page.tsx`

## Source references

- OpenCode publishes official assets and brand guidance at https://opencode.ai/brand and in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode.
- Pi's project home and source are https://pi.dev/ and https://github.com/earendil-works/pi.

Prepared with AI assistance after inspecting current Cribble main, its agent-label normalization, icon component/call sites, repository issue/PR inventory, and the projects' authoritative public sources.

title: Fix globe drag selection and add minimal orbit, zoom, pan, and spatial ambience
body:
## User problem

The homepage globe currently has two related interaction and presentation limitations.

### 1. Drag can select the pilot username chip

While dragging the Earth, the floating `@username · CITY` indicator can occasionally become text-selected. Once selection starts, the browser owns the gesture and globe rotation becomes unreliable or stops.

Current source at `b57a99a5d569336a32422c5cb4490995adc3ac3c` uses a dedicated circular drag hit surface and window-level pointer movement, but the username chip does not explicitly disable selection. The drag path also does not hold pointer capture or suppress `selectstart` for an active globe gesture.

### 2. The globe needs a minimal map-like control vocabulary and a more immersive spatial scene

Rotation is currently longitude-only. I want to inspect the world with a deliberately small interaction set:

- orbit in two axes;
- bounded zoom;
- bounded pan;
- reset/home;
- nothing resembling a full map toolbar.

The surrounding scene should feel deeper and more alive without competing with the homepage copy. Add restrained spatial ambience:

- a small distant Sun;
- a few stars;
- sparse asteroids/debris;
- a small number of “starcloud” data-center objects or orbital infrastructure;
- selected ambience may bleed outside the existing Earth canvas and sit behind hero text, but must preserve reading contrast and pointer behavior.

## Product principle

**Earth remains the hero; space is negative space with a few meaningful objects.**

This should not become a particle field, game HUD, generic sci-fi wallpaper, or full GIS interface. It should retain Cribble's minimal, editorial hierarchy.

## Proposed staged delivery

This issue is intentionally staged. Each phase should be independently reviewable and must not be collapsed into one large visual rewrite.

### Phase A — Fix drag ownership and text selection

- Apply `user-select: none` to the globe interaction region and pilot chip while preserving normal selection in the hero copy.
- Prevent `selectstart` only during an active globe gesture.
- Use pointer capture on pointer-down and release it on pointer-up/cancel where supported.
- Preserve an active drag when the pointer crosses the pilot chip or leaves the circular hit area.
- Restore cursor and interaction state on `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, blur, unmount, and lost capture.
- Do not block links, text selection outside the globe, page scrolling, or assistive technology.

Acceptance:

- Repeated dragging through the pilot username never highlights text.
- Horizontal, vertical, and diagonal drag paths remain owned until release/cancel.
- Releasing outside the globe cannot leave a stuck grabbing cursor.
- Touch page scrolling remains available outside an intentional globe gesture.
- Regression tests cover selection, pointer capture/loss, chip crossing, cancellation, and cleanup.

### Phase B — Minimal map-like controls

#### Pointer and touch grammar

- **Primary drag:** orbit longitude and latitude.
- **Wheel / trackpad pinch:** zoom.
- **Two-finger drag on touch:** pan.
- **Desktop pan:** modifier + drag (for example Shift+drag) or secondary drag; choose one after browser/input testing.
- **Double click/tap or one minimal home button:** reset to the authored hero framing.
- No visible +/-/compass toolbar unless accessibility testing demonstrates it is necessary. A small reset affordance is acceptable.

#### Bounds and feel

- Clamp latitude before the poles so the camera cannot flip.
- Use bounded zoom with an authored home value; prevent clipping through atmosphere, satellites, and geometry.
- Bound pan so Earth cannot be lost or parked over the primary copy/CTA.
- Direct manipulation should be 1:1 while held, with short restrained inertia only for orbit.
- Auto-spin pauses during interaction and resumes smoothly after a quiet delay.
- Preserve the current scroll choreography, feature-aware framing work, theme transition, offscreen parking, and reduced-motion behavior.
- `Esc` and reset/home restore the canonical composition.

Accessibility:

- Provide keyboard-accessible reset and compact instructions such as “drag to orbit · wheel/pinch to zoom · two fingers/Shift+drag to pan.”
- Do not trap wheel or touch scrolling when the gesture is not clearly operating the globe.
- Reduced motion disables autonomous motion and inertia, but keeps direct manipulation.

Acceptance:

- Orbit, zoom, pan, and reset work on mouse, trackpad, and touch without accidental page-scroll capture.
- Camera state stays finite and within declared bounds under adversarial wheel/pointer input.
- No pole flip, camera clipping, lost Earth, or stuck gesture state.
- Back/Forward and homepage scroll behavior remain unchanged.
- Controls remain minimal and do not add a persistent map toolbar.

### Phase C — Minimal spatial ambience

Build ambience as a separate background layer or bounded extension seam rather than inflating the Earth renderer by default.

#### Distant Sun

- Small, off-axis, and visibly distant.
- Position should agree with the Earth's existing key-light/terminator direction.
- One restrained halo; no lens-flare stack or large blur shell.
- May sit outside the globe footprint and behind hero copy, but never reduce text/CTA contrast below WCAG AA.

#### Stars

- Sparse, deterministic, and depth-separated.
- Prefer one static texture, one CSS layer, or one instanced draw—not hundreds of DOM nodes.
- Parallax must be subtle and disabled by reduced motion.

#### Starcloud data centers / orbital infrastructure

- Add only a few recognizable silhouettes or nodes.
- They should communicate distributed AI infrastructure rather than decoration alone.
- Use bounded activity pulses; no private usage data or misleading real-time claims.
- Avoid visual similarity to the existing satellites unless hierarchy is clear.

#### Asteroids and debris

- Very sparse foreground/background objects with deterministic trajectories.
- Keep them away from copy, CTA, and globe controls.
- No collision gameplay, particle spray, or high-frequency motion.
- Objects bleeding behind text must be low-contrast and non-interactive.

Acceptance:

- Earth remains the strongest object in every sampled frame.
- Hero heading, body copy, and CTA remain readable across dark/light themes, desktop/mobile, and a full ambience cycle.
- Ambient layers use `pointer-events: none` and never interrupt globe gestures or links.
- Reduced motion yields a composed static scene, not an empty or broken one.
- Mobile may omit/degrade ambience according to an explicit quality budget.

## Performance contract

Use the revision-bound Earth audit from task `t_5545a9dc` as reconnaissance, not a certifying baseline. The current implementation already caps Earth DPR at 1.5, uses resting scissor, merged/instanced geometry, and parks WebGL/CSS animation offscreen. Preserve those strengths.

Before/after gate on a quiet physical display:

- hardware renderer and exact Earth/backdrop drawing buffers proven;
- 100,000 presented frames for certifying desktop and target-mobile rows, or shorter rows explicitly labeled smoke;
- report average FPS, 0.001% low, median/p95/p99/p99.9/worst and >25/>50/>100 ms counts;
- no regression beyond 0.10 ms median, 0.25 ms p95, or 0.50 ms p99 for Phase A/B;
- no new attributable >50 ms frames;
- ambient Phase C gets a separately approved GPU/fill budget;
- no uncapped DPR3, additional full-screen blur shells, dense particles, per-frame React state, hundreds of DOM stars, or unbounded transparent overdraw;
- all WebGL and CSS loops park when offscreen/hidden;
- reduced-motion row has no autonomous ambient animation.

## Visual evidence contract

For each phase, capture:

- desktop dark and light;
- mobile portrait;
- reduced motion;
- full Earth rotation;
- orbit/zoom/pan/reset interaction video;
- Sun/ambience positions at their brightest/closest text overlap;
- labels-hidden before/after visual comparison.

Reject any version where spectacle overtakes the Earth or copy.

## Non-goals

- Full GIS/map navigation
- Search, geocoding, place labels, compass, or map layers
- Unbounded free camera
- Collision/gameplay systems
- Dense star/particle fields
- Live private token/activity visualization
- Replacing the current Earth renderer or scroll story
- Adding every requested visual object in the first PR

title: Fraud detection for leaderboard & token abuse
body:
## What & why

The ingest routes already enforce **hard bounds** (per-event duration caps, a rolling 24h active-time/visit ceiling, a domain allowlist, per-record token caps, freshness windows). Those stop the crudest inflation, but a patient scripted extension can sit *just under* every cap and climb the board on fabricated activity, and a client can backfill impossible token totals onto the Burn Board.

This PR adds the missing **detection layer**: it runs over what actually landed in the database, looks for the behavioural signatures the hard caps can't express, raises deduped flags, alerts staff, and gives staff a review queue to confirm (optionally suspending) or dismiss.

## How it works

**Detection engine — `src/lib/fraudDetection.ts` (pure, deterministic)**
Seven evidence-based detectors, biased for precision (each carries the raw numbers it fired on, for audit):

| Signal | Surface | Catches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `activity_ceiling_pinning` | activity | Banking >=90% of the 16h/day active ceiling day after day |
| `impossible_concurrency` | activity | Verified active time far exceeding the day's wall-clock span (parallel forged streams) |
| `visit_flooding` | activity | Near-ceiling visits with negligible active time (flat 40-pt visit padding) |
| `uniform_duration_padding` | activity | One duration value dominating a large heartbeat sample (scripted client) |
| `token_impossible_rate` | token | Sustained billions of tokens/day — not a real agent workload |
| `token_spike` | token | A single day dwarfing the user's own median (backfilled dump) |
| `token_cost_mismatch` | token | Huge token totals with implausible cost/token (gaming the cost-ordered Burn Board) |

`assessUserFraud` rolls signals up per category into a capped 0–100 risk score, a level band, and a stable dedupe fingerprint.

**Persistence & orchestration — `src/lib/fraudDetectionServer.ts` + migration 061**
- `fraud_flags` table (service-role only): one row per `(user, category)`, deduped by fingerprint, with `open`/`confirmed`/`dismissed` triage state and an audit-friendly signal snapshot.
- The service layer fetches a user's recent activity + token history, assesses it, upserts flags (a recurring pattern refreshes the row and bumps `detection_count` **without** resurrecting a staff decision), and alerts every staff member once per newly-opened flag. Everything is best-effort and never throws.
- `sweepFraudSignals` scans the competitive-board candidate set (top scorers + Burn Board opt-ins) and **piggybacks the existing `leaderboard-integrity` cron** (same Vercel cron-budget reason as the sponsor sweep).

**Staff surface**
- `abuse.review` staff action at the **moderator floor**.
- `GET /api/admin/abuse` — worst-first queue with per-status counts and the flagged account's identity.
- `POST /api/admin/abuse/[id]/review` — confirm/dismiss (audit-first, target-guarded, status-guarded, reason required), with optional **suspend on confirm** via the shared moderation path.
- `/admin/abuse` review-queue page (mirrors the Teams queue) + a nav entry under **Review**.

## Testing

- **31 new unit tests** (engine + server layer with a mock Supabase client). Full suite: **990 passing** (was 959).
- `typecheck`, `lint`, `audit:prod` (0 vulns), and `next build` all green; new routes compile (`/admin/abuse`, `/api/admin/abuse`, `/api/admin/abuse/[id]/review`).
- Ran the real engine over synthetic histories — a heavy-but-human user is **CLEAN** (no false positives), while an activity cheater and a token cheater both hit **critical** risk with the expected signals:

```
=== Clean heavy-but-human user ===
  verdict: CLEAN — no signals fired

=== Activity cheater (scripted extension) ===
  [activity] level=critical risk=100/100
     - (high, +58) activity_ceiling_pinning: Banked >=90% of the 16h/day active-time ceiling on 6 day(s)
     - (high, +55) impossible_concurrency: Active time exceeded the wall-clock window 2.50x — parallel activity streams

=== Token cheater (fabricated Burn Board) ===
  [token] level=critical risk=100/100
     - (high, +50) token_impossible_rate: Reported >=2,000,000,000 tokens/day on 2 day(s)
     - (high, +35) token_spike: One day reported 2609x the median token day — backfilled spike
     - (medium, +20) token_cost_mismatch: Reported 5,804,200,000 tokens for $12.00 — implausible cost/token
```

> A screenshot of the review-queue UI (rendered with the real admin component kit) is attached to the companion PR on the fork. Live admin-panel interaction needs an authenticated staff session against a real Supabase, so the queue was rendered via a temporary preview route (removed before commit). The detection engine — the novel, high-risk part — is proven end-to-end by unit tests and the runtime demo above.

## Deploy notes

- Apply `migrations/061_fraud_flags.sql` (creates the table; ends with `NOTIFY pgrst`). Thresholds live in `DEFAULT_FRAUD_POLICY` and can be tuned without schema changes.
- No new cron entry needed — the sweep rides the existing `/api/cron/leaderboard-integrity` schedule.

## Possible follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Cross-account device-sharing detection (multiple accounts on one `device_uuid`).
- A fraud-flag panel on the per-user admin dossier.
- Auto-exclusion of `confirmed` accounts from the canonical leaderboard ranker.

title: GitHub and X logins share users.twitter_id without a provider discriminator
body:
GitHub and X OAuth both resolve accounts through `users.twitter_id` using the raw numeric provider id, with no provider discriminator.

GitHub ids and X ids occupy overlapping integer ranges. A login on one provider can match a row created by the other, so the two identities are treated as the same Cribble account.

**Suggested fix.** Namespace stored ids (`github:{id}` / `x:{id}`), prefix existing rows from the public avatar host, and refuse to let X claim an ambiguous unprefixed legacy row. A patch with tests is in QuarkOS/Cribble#2 (`migrations/061_auth_provider_and_session_hash.sql`, `src/lib/authAccount.ts`).

No reproduction steps in this report. Happy to walk through the lookup change on a private channel if useful.

title: Session secrets stored in plaintext; leftover routes skip the shared session gate
body:
`user_sessions.session_token` stores the cookie secret in plaintext. Device sync tokens and agent API keys already store SHA-256. A database read of `user_sessions` is enough to mint a working `cribble_session` cookie.

Two leftover routes also skip `getSessionUserId`:
- `/api/user/score`
- `/api/extension/devices`

Those private lookups do not apply the banned-account gate. Devices POST also skips `register_user_device` and never issues a sync token, so it does not share the transfer/revoke semantics of `/api/extension/sync`.

**Suggested fix.** Hash the session secret at rest (cookie stays plaintext, lookup hashes first). Point both leftover routes at `getSessionUserId`. Register devices through the existing RPC and return a one-time hashed token. Patch with tests: QuarkOS/Cribble#2.

Apply `migrations/061_auth_provider_and_session_hash.sql` with the session-hash half so existing cookies keep working.

title: Device sync token is delivered over window.postMessage
body:
`notifyDeviceRegistered` still puts the newly issued device sync token on `window.postMessage` targeted at the page origin (`src/lib/extensionBridge.ts`).

Any other extension with a content script on cribble.dev can observe that message and reuse the token against `/api/extension/sync`. Page-origin checks do not stop same-origin content scripts.

**Suggested fix.** Deliver the token with `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` to a pinned extension id, and declare `externally_connectable` for cribble.dev in the official extension. Do not put the long-lived token on `window.postMessage`.

This needs a coordinated change in the extension repo. Changing only the website handshake would break linking for current clients, so it is not in QuarkOS/Cribble#2.

Related ingest hardening that is in that PR: per-device distributed rate limit on `/api/extension/sync`, trusted IP headers for rate-limit buckets, and CORS no longer advertising `x-cron-secret`.

title: Replace leaderboard See stats new-tab flow with an in-UI tracker popup
body:
## Problem

The leaderboard's **see stats** control opens GoatCounter in a new tab. That takes people out of the arena for data that can fit naturally in Cribble's existing modal UI.

## What the ccusage feedback changed

The maintainer response on ccusage/ccusage#1650 rejected a broad discovery proposal because its safety contract was unfinished. The proposed walker had no hard resource limits and could return partial results after read errors. Redaction, alias handling, supported roots, and preview behavior were still undefined.

The relevant lesson here is simple: an external-data feature needs a finite contract before it ships. For this popup that means:

- fetch one configured public tracker page; do not crawl
- cap the decoded response at 256 KiB and time out after 5 seconds
- expose a versioned snapshot with at most 10 paths
- strip query strings and fragments, and replace referral codes with `/join/[code]`
- reject malformed or partially parsed snapshots instead of returning guessed data
- keep the current first-party live/12h pulse as the source for online counts
- link to GoatCounter rather than iframe it

## Proposed UX

1. The visitor ticker stays on `/leaderboard`.
2. **see stats** opens an `ARENA STATS` dialog using the same glass treatment as Cribble's feedback modal.
3. While open, it refreshes:
   - live and last-12h pulse from `/api/analytics/visitors`
   - period visits and top paths from `/api/analytics/tracker`
4. The footer links to the full public GoatCounter dashboard.
5. Escape, backdrop click, the header close control, and the footer close button dismiss the dialog. Focus enters the dialog and returns to the trigger.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The leaderboard no longer navigates away when **see stats** is clicked.
- [ ] Tracker responses are byte-bounded, timed out, schema-versioned, path-redacted, and fail closed.
- [ ] A failed tracker refresh shows an explicit unavailable state, not stale or partial data.
- [ ] The canonical GoatCounter dashboard remains one click away.
- [ ] Desktop and mobile layouts remain usable.

## Current PR audit (2026-08-31)

None of Kevin's prior Cribble PRs have merged.

Open on `Birdabo404/Cribble`: #48, #49, #52, #55, #57, #59, #62, #64, #66, #68, #70, #73, #76. PR #53 was closed without merge after #55 superseded it.

title: Add Antigravity CLI support to terminal usage tracking
body:
# Add Antigravity CLI support to terminal usage tracking

## Summary

Cribble's current terminal usage counter recognizes the legacy **Gemini CLI** (`gemini-cli`) and its aliases, but does not appear to correctly identify or attribute usage from the newer **Antigravity CLI** (`agy` / `antigravity-cli`).

Gemini CLI is no longer the production CLI. Antigravity CLI supersedes it while continuing to use the same `~/.gemini` base directory. Because the two CLIs share parts of their storage layout but use different CLI-specific configuration and data paths, detecting only the legacy Gemini aliases/configuration can cause current Antigravity usage to be missed or incorrectly attributed.

The terminal usage collector should be updated to explicitly recognize Antigravity CLI and distinguish its data/configuration from legacy Gemini CLI where necessary.

---

## Current Implementation

Cribble currently tracks Gemini CLI as one of several AI tools in its token-based leaderboard system.

### 1. Agent Registration and Aliasing

Gemini CLI is registered as a harness brand in:

```text
src/lib/harnessBrands.ts
```

with:

- **Label:** `Gemini CLI`
- **Aliases:** `gemini`, `gemini-cli`
- **Visual branding:** custom gradient, accent color (`#8B9DFF`), and icon

At present, these aliases only account for the older Gemini CLI naming.

### 2. Token Breakdown Tracking

Per-agent usage is collected through the `agent_breakdown` structure, including:

```text
name
totalTokens
```

For example:

```text
name: gemini-cli
name: gemini
```

The collected values are aggregated and sorted by token usage.

### 3. Normalization and Labeling

Agent IDs are normalized to lowercase/hyphenated identifiers through:

```typescript
normalizeAgentId()
```

Collector IDs such as:

```text
gemini-cli
```

are then converted into user-facing labels through:

```typescript
tokenAgentLabel()
```

### 4. AI Board Integration

Gemini CLI usage is currently mapped into the AI leaderboard using `AGENT_AI_TOOL_NAMES`:

```typescript
'gemini': 'Gemini',
'gemini-cli': 'Gemini',
```

Both aliases therefore resolve to the same `Gemini` leaderboard entry.

There is currently no equivalent mapping for Antigravity identifiers such as:

```text
agy
antigravity
antigravity-cli
```

### 5. Cost / Burn Tracking

Cribble also tracks monetary cost associated with CLI usage through:

```typescript
burnByToolName()
```

Sibling agent IDs are folded together when calculating burn.

Any Antigravity identifiers introduced by the collector should therefore also be handled by the appropriate normalization/folding logic.

---

## Problem

The current implementation is based on the legacy Gemini CLI and its aliases:

```text
gemini
gemini-cli
```

However, the current production CLI is **Antigravity CLI**.

Antigravity CLI and Gemini CLI share the same base Gemini configuration directory:

```text
~/.gemini
```

but they do **not** use an identical storage layout.

This means checking for `~/.gemini` alone is not sufficient to determine whether usage belongs to legacy Gemini CLI or Antigravity CLI.

---

## Gemini CLI vs. Antigravity CLI Storage

### Shared Base Directory

Both tools use:

```text
~/.gemini/
```

They may also share global instructions such as:

```text
~/.gemini/GEMINI.md
```

This allows existing Gemini configuration/history to remain available during migration.

### Antigravity-Specific Storage

Antigravity introduces its own paths beneath the shared directory, including:

```text
~/.gemini/antigravity/
~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/
~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/
```

Antigravity CLI-specific settings can be stored under:

```text
~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json
```

Legacy Gemini CLI configuration can therefore coexist with Antigravity-specific configuration beneath the same `~/.gemini` root.

---

## Windows Example

A working Antigravity installation on Windows shows the following structure.

### Gemini / Antigravity Data

```text
C:\Users\labs\.gemini
├── antigravity
├── antigravity-backup
├── antigravity-cli
├── antigravity-ide
├── config
├── history
├── skills
├── tmp
├── _GEMINI.md
├── GEMINI.md
├── google_accounts.json
├── installation_id
├── oauth_creds.json
├── projects.json
├── settings.json
├── state.json
├── trustedFolders.json
└── antigravity
    ├── annotations
    ├── bin
    └── brain
```

### Antigravity CLI Binary

Antigravity also installs the `agy` CLI separately:

```text
C:\Users\labs\AppData\Local\agy
└── bin
    └── agy.exe
```

This provides another useful signal for detecting Antigravity CLI independently of the shared `.gemini` directory.

---

## Expected Behavior

Cribble should recognize current Antigravity CLI usage in addition to legacy Gemini CLI usage.

At minimum, the implementation should account for Antigravity identifiers such as:

```text
agy
antigravity
antigravity-cli
```

and inspect Antigravity-specific storage when determining the source of usage.

Possible Antigravity indicators include:

```text
~/.gemini/antigravity/
~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/
~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/
```

On Windows, the CLI installation may additionally be detected at:

```text
%LOCALAPPDATA%\agy\bin\agy.exe
```

Detection should **not** rely exclusively on the existence of:

```text
~/.gemini
```

because this directory is shared between legacy Gemini CLI and Antigravity.

---

## Proposed Changes

- [ ] Add Antigravity CLI as a recognized harness/tool.
- [ ] Add appropriate aliases, potentially including:
  - `agy`
  - `antigravity`
  - `antigravity-cli`
- [ ] Update collector detection to recognize Antigravity-specific configuration/data paths.
- [ ] Avoid treating the shared `~/.gemini` directory alone as proof of legacy Gemini CLI usage.
- [ ] Add Antigravity mappings to `AGENT_AI_TOOL_NAMES`.
- [ ] Update `tokenAgentLabel()` / normalization logic where necessary.
- [ ] Update `burnByToolName()` so Antigravity usage is attributed correctly.
- [ ] Preserve compatibility with existing/legacy `gemini` and `gemini-cli` data.
- [ ] Add Windows detection/support for `%LOCALAPPDATA%\agy` where relevant.
- [ ] Verify equivalent Antigravity paths on macOS/Linux.
- [ ] Add tests covering systems where Gemini CLI and Antigravity configuration coexist.

---

## Suggested Alias Mapping

The exact leaderboard naming is a product decision, but the collector should at least normalize the new identifiers consistently.

For example:

```typescript
'gemini': 'Gemini',
'gemini-cli': 'Gemini',
'antigravity': 'Antigravity',
'antigravity-cli': 'Antigravity',
'agy': 'Antigravity',
```

Alternatively, if Gemini and Antigravity usage are intentionally meant to remain under a single historical leaderboard entry, all aliases could resolve to the same tool.

The important part is that **Antigravity CLI usage is actually detected and counted**, rather than relying solely on aliases associated with the retired Gemini CLI.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Running Antigravity CLI results in terminal/token usage being counted by Cribble.
2. `agy`, `antigravity`, and/or `antigravity-cli` collector identifiers are normalized correctly.
3. Antigravity usage appears under the intended leaderboard entry.
4. Antigravity usage is included in cost/burn calculations.
5. Existing Gemini CLI usage remains backwards-compatible.
6. A shared `~/.gemini` directory does not cause Antigravity usage to be incorrectly classified as legacy Gemini CLI.
7. Systems containing both legacy Gemini configuration and Antigravity configuration are handled correctly.
8. Detection works with the Antigravity-specific Windows paths demonstrated above.
9. Tests cover both legacy Gemini CLI and current Antigravity CLI layouts.

---

## References

- [Antigravity CLI migration documentation](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/gcli-migration/)
- [Antigravity CLI usage documentation](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/using/)
- [Firebase Gemini CLI extension documentation](https://firebase.google.com/docs/ai-assistance/gcli-extension)
- [Code Agent Swarm — How to Use Antigravity CLI](https://www.codeagentswarm.com/en/guides/how-to-use-antigravity-cli)

---

## Additional Context

This is primarily a compatibility/update issue rather than a request to remove Gemini CLI support.

Legacy Gemini CLI aliases should remain supported for historical data and users who still have older configuration present. The key change is to make Antigravity CLI a first-class recognized source so that Cribble's terminal usage counter reflects usage from the currently deployed CLI.

title: bag: manifest redesign
body:
## Summary

The bag is a manifest, not a shop: a count-first ledger of what the pilot carries. Plates are register rows and badges are inventory slots on one sheet of paper, with a spec sheet for the selected item and exactly one item alive on screen — the single signal-filled EQUIP action. Everything else (selection, focus, status, class) is carried by ink, rarity colour and registration marks.

## What changed

- `src/app/(app)/bag/page.tsx` shrinks from ~1.4k lines to composition + state; the pieces live in `src/components/bag/`:
  - `ManifestHeader` (title block, telemetry, sync cell with RETRY), `CompartmentIndex` (tabs, owned/rarity filters and search as a rail from lg, a strip below)
  - `PlateRegister` / `PlateRow` (fixed-width ledger columns per breakpoint), `BadgeRegister` / `BadgeSlot` (4 / 5 / 6 across, 14px index strip above the sprite)
  - `PlateSpecSheet` / `BadgeSpecSheet` (preview, dt/dd spec list, one action, barcode), `SpecDrawer` (mobile bottom sheet on a `--bag-veil` backdrop), `LoadoutStrip` (mobile sticky strip: 64x16 thumb + name/status as one open-sheet button, one action)
  - `RegMarks`, `Barcode`, `RegisterEmpty`, `RegisterLoading`, `bagModel` (+ tests), `useBagData`, `useMinWidth`, `manifestChrome` / `registerChrome` (shared class recipes)
- `src/app/globals.css`: a scoped `/* ==== BAG MANIFEST ==== */` block — `--bag-paper/ink/mute/line/line-soft/well/signal/signal-text/on-signal/focus/veil/tap` and the micro/label/copy font tokens, with a light-mode block that re-pins `--r-rare` / `--r-legendary` and a `md+` block that divides the micro sizes and the tap floor by 0.9 to undo `.page-zoom-out`.
- `src/app/(app)/bag/layout.tsx`: page metadata.

## Design rules

- No radius, no shadow, no glow. Hairlines, paper, ink, regmarks.
- Every colour and size goes through a `--bag-*` token; light mode re-pins primitives inside `html.light .bag-manifest` only.
- One filled action per screen (EQUIP on `--bag-signal` with `--bag-on-signal` text). Signal as text or a thin mark uses `--bag-signal-text` (5.00:1 on paper). Selection and keyboard focus use `--bag-focus` (= ink): solid outline when selected, dashed on focus-visible. The equipped row's 2px left bar is the only other signal mark.
- Column widths are fixed per breakpoint, never content-driven; NAME is the only flexible track and has a floor (96px below md, 120px from md) so the register never overflows.

## Fixes shipped alongside

- Safe-area bottom padding on the frame; sticky ladders use `calc(var(--nav-topbar-h) + 1px)` (and `/0.9` at md+) so the strip's hairline never tucks under the top bar.
- Sync-failed state: rows render `?` "status unknown" in mute (no dither) instead of guessing LOCKED, matching the sheet's `UNKNOWN · SYNC FAILED`; the header RETRY is a real tap-floor button.
- Contrast in light mode: GET IT / EQUIPPED text 5.00:1, RARE 7.30:1, LEGENDARY 8.37:1, EPIC 5.20:1, MYTHIC 6.07:1, COMMON 4.67:1 on paper.
- Tap targets: every control inside the manifest sits on `min-h-[var(--bag-tap)]` (44px effective at every width, including under the 0.9 zoom).
- Keyboard: one listbox per register with a 2D arrow stride read from the live column count; `aria-controls` only on the selected tab (the inactive panel is not rendered); visible `focus-within` ring on the search well.
- Badge loading gated on `achievements === null || achievementsState === 'loading'`.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run lint` clean, `npm run test:run` 139 files / 1894 tests passing (includes `bagModel.test.ts`).
- Headless-browser harness (Brave over CDP, `/api/user/*` mocked, dark + light, nav rail on) — captures under `/tmp/bag-review/after/`:
  - `plates-{375x812,768x1024,1280x800,1536x960}-{dark,light}.png`, `plates-stowed-375x812-*.png`, `plates-locked-{375x812,768x1024,1280x800,1536x960}-*.png`
  - `badges-{375x812,768x1024,1280x800,1536x960}-{dark,light}.png`
  - `drawer-375x812-{dark,light}.png`, `strip-stuck-375x812-{dark,light}.png`
  - `error-1280x800-{dark,light}.png`, `error-375x812-dark.png`
  - `navtop-scrolled-{768x1024,1280x800}-dark.png`, `measurements.json`
- Measurements (CSS px):
  - NAME column: 174.2 at 375 · 136.0 at 768 · 144.9 at 1280 · 144.9 at 1536 (207.1 at 768 with the top nav). Floors: ≥96 below md, ≥120 from md.
  - Register horizontal overflow: 0 at every viewport (the 4px reported by a naive scrollWidth check is the decorative regmark pseudo-elements, which are designed to sit 4px outside the frame; with them hidden it is exactly 0).
  - Smallest effective font inside `.bag-manifest` at 1280: 10.0px (every readable node ≥10 after the 0.9 zoom; the only smaller nodes are the `aria-hidden` ASCII footer mark and the ticker's decorative notes).
  - Smallest interactive box at 768: 44px (28 controls on plates, 39 on badges, zero violations). At 375: zero violations.
  - Signal-filled elements on screen: exactly 1 (the EQUIP button) at 768 and 1280 when the selected plate is owned-but-stowed; 0 when it is equipped (UNEQUIP is hollow), locked (GET IT is a signal-text outline), or on the badges tab. The equipped row's 2px bar is the only other signal-coloured mark.
  - Light-mode contrast (computed colours on `rgb(252 251 247)`): GET IT text + border `rgb(194 65 12)` 5.00:1 · EQUIPPED 5.00:1 · RARE `rgb(7 89 133)` 7.30:1 · LEGENDARY `rgb(113 63 18)` 8.37:1.
  - Error state: header `SYNC FAILED · RETRY` (RETRY 53x44), rows `?` with `aria-label` "…, status unknown, …", zero dithers, sheet `UNKNOWN · SYNC FAILED` with `EQUIP UNAVAILABLE` disabled.
  - Below md: loadout strip mounted and visible, sticky at `57px`, buttons "Open spec sheet" 247x54 and UNEQUIP 88x44, thumb 64x16, LOCKED never printed twice. From md: strip not mounted, track-3 sheet mounted (15 row thumbs + 2 sheet previews = 17 `PlateLayer`s, no hidden duplicates).

## Deviations from the review spec

- Status column at xl stays glyph-only. With the 220 / 380 tracks and `max-w-6xl`, the register cell is 462px from 1280; a widened status track for the inline label would leave NAME at ~89px, under the 120px floor. The label lives in the row's `aria-label`, the strip and the sheet.
- Badge grid tops out at 6 columns (`grid-cols-4 sm:grid-cols-5 lg:grid-cols-6`) instead of 8 at xl. Eight columns in a 462px register are 57px cells, which clip every name to six characters; six keeps slots at 72–78px from md up, matching 768.

## Follow-ups

- The VFD now-playing ticker (`AppShell` / `NowPlayingTicker`) overlaps the sheet's action row at lg/xl. App-level; not touched here.
- Badge names below `sm` are hidden in the grid and carried by the strip and the sheet only.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large front-end refactor of a user-facing equip flow; regressions could affect plate selection, equip UX, or signed-out/error states, though behavior is constrained to existing APIs and covered by new model tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the monolithic **Bag** page with a **manifest-style** inventory: count-first header, compartment index (tabs + filters), ledger **register** for plates / slot grid for badges, and a sticky **spec sheet** (desktop) or **loadout strip + drawer** (mobile). Plate equip/unequip still uses the existing profile PATCH; no API changes.
> 
> Logic moves into **`bagModel`** (filters, status, serials) with Vitest coverage, **`useBagData`** (fetch, idle achievement prefetch, optimistic equip), and a new **`src/components/bag/`** UI kit. **`globals.css`** adds scoped `--bag-*` tokens, light/dark substrates, and register/sheet chrome.
> 
> **Behavioral fixes:** failed cosmetics sync surfaces **`SYNC FAILED` + RETRY**, blocks equip, and shows **status unknown** instead of implying everything is locked; usable plates label as **STOWED** in the new status copy.

- **Provisioning** (`scripts/setup-dodo.ts`): products (20-year subscription period so plans renew), `PROPLATES` discount, filtered webhook endpoint; `--write-env` emits the `DODO_*` block. Polar scripts removed.

title: feat(plates): Season 01 scene plates on sale, launch drop retired
body:
## What ships

- **Four Season 01 plates on sale**, each epic at $5.99 with the SEASON 01 tag: **Always Open**, **Noodle Dragon**, **Touch Grass** and **Peer Review**. They're painted art cut into layers (1.3 MB of WebP under `public/plates/season-01/`), rendered by a new `scene` render kind (`PlateScene` + CSS module). Each scene picks its layout by the plate's aspect ratio, so the subject is placed per surface (featured stage, cards and podium, mobile rows, desktop strips) instead of being cover-cropped. Animations are transform/opacity only, and the existing reduced-motion freeze covers them.
- **Screen Time and Cooldown are marked unavailable.** They close the PLATES grid as sealed cards with no buy button. They aren't catalog plates, so nothing can sell, grant or equip them.
- **The six launch plates are retired from sale:** Synthwave Grid, Deep Space, Terminal Rain, Cherry Blossom, Keyboard Cat and Season 01: Ignition. Owners keep them and can still equip them; the bag labels them `SHOP — retired`. Checkout refuses them (they're unpriced now). Grant, sync and webhook handling don't check price, so late webhooks and refunds for them still resolve.
- Always Open replaces Ignition on the featured rail and on the landing page plate showcase.
- `plateTint()` replaces the css-only `accent`/`bleed` reads in the leaderboard row and `PlatePreview`.

The new plates need live Dodo products, and production's `DODO_PLATE_PRODUCT_MAP` must be updated. Until then their buy buttons return "Unknown plate". Production's Dodo variables are Sensitive (write-only), so the map has to be replaced in full. `setup-dodo` now includes the retired plates' existing products in the map it prints, so its output is safe to paste as the replacement.

```sh
# file holding DODO_PAYMENTS_ENVIRONMENT=live_mode and DODO_PAYMENTS_API_KEY=<live key>
DODO_SETUP_ENV_FILE=~/.cribble-dodo-live.env NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL= npx vite-node scripts/setup-dodo.ts --check
DODO_SETUP_ENV_FILE=~/.cribble-dodo-live.env NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL= npx vite-node scripts/setup-dodo.ts --live
# then set the printed DODO_PLATE_PRODUCT_MAP on Vercel production
```

A test-mode dry run already passes: 4 plates missing, and all 6 retired plates kept in the map.

## Verification

- `vitest run`: 1850 passing. `tsc --noEmit` and eslint are clean.
- Rendered in the running app: the shop grid (4 for sale, 2 unavailable), the featured stage with Always Open, and each plate cloned into desktop-row, mobile-row, podium and card sizes. The mobile-row layouts move every subject left of the score.
